I made no changes. The only place the new code compares a role is `filter-users.ts:14`, and I don't think that breaks the rule as written.

```ts
if (role !== 'ALL' && user.role !== role) {
```

This is a list filter on the rows the API returned, not an access check. The rule is about deciding what the current user may do. `checkAccess` and `<Authorization>` only evaluate the logged-in user (`useUser()` inside `useAuthorization`), so they can't decide whether a different row matches the selected role. The other `user.role` reference, in `export-users-csv.ts`, only writes the value into the CSV. `users-list.tsx` has no role comparison.

If you still want that comparison out of the client, the clean option is to have the users API take a `role` query parameter and filter on the server. Then `filter-users.ts` only does the search matching. I haven't made that change because it means touching the API layer in `src/features/users/api/`, and it's your call whether to do it. Tests, lint and the app were not run, as you asked.
